---
title: "Examples"
---

These examples show RayTraceHeatTransfer.jl at work, from a first grey problem to a million-element benchmark.

## Participating media in 2D

- [Example 1 — 2D Grey Participating Medium](example-01.qmd): the basic workflow, validated against Crosbie and Schrenker.
- [Example 2 — Spectral Greenhouse Atmosphere](example-02.qmd): a spectral problem with adaptive spectral bins.
- [Example 3 — Line Spectrum vs Line-by-Line Reference](example-03.qmd): a synthetic line spectrum against an independent line-by-line solution.
- [Example 4 — Anisotropic Scattering vs a Discrete-Ordinates Reference](example-04.qmd): directional scattering and reflection on angular bins.
- [Example 5 — Circular Enclosure from Triangular Elements](example-05.qmd): curved geometry built from triangles.
- [Example 6 — Five-Pointed Star with a Volumetric Heat Source](example-06.qmd): a geometry generated by a loop, heated from within like a combustion chamber.

## Surfaces in 3D

- [Example 7 — 3D Surface Enclosure](example-07.qmd): analytical view factors in a cube.
- [Example 8 — Triangulated Icosphere](example-08.qmd): convergence on a sphere built from triangles.
- [Example 9 — Mixed Triangular and Quadrilateral Faces](example-09.qmd): meshes mixing both element shapes.
- [Example 10 — Non-Convex Enclosure: an L-Shaped Duct](example-10.qmd): ray tracing where surfaces shadow each other.

## Accuracy and scale

- [Example 11 — Convergence in Rays and Mesh](example-11.qmd): how the solution converges with more rays and a finer mesh.
- [Example 12 — Large Scale: a Million Elements](example-12.qmd): a billion rays and a million elements, against the diffusion approximation.
